The German National People's Party ( German : Deutschnationale Volkspartei , DNVP ) was a national-conservative and monarchist political party in Germany during the Weimar Republic . [ 26 ] [ 27 ] Before the rise of the Nazi Party , it was the major nationalist party in Weimar Germany. It was an alliance of conservative , nationalist , monarchist, völkisch , and antisemitic elements supported by the Pan-German League . [ 28 ] Ideologically, the party was described as subscribing to authoritarian conservatism , [ 29 ] German nationalism, [ 30 ] and monarchism. [ 31 ] [ 32 ] Until 1931, the party also advocated for national liberal [ 33 ] [ 34 ] [ 35 ] [ 36 ] and protectionist economic policies, [ 37 ] [ 38 ] embracing corporatist economic policies from 1931 onwards. [ 39 ] Some members like the populist media mogul Alfred Hugenberg embraced economic nationalism and statism . [ 40 ] It held anti-communist , anti-Catholic , [ 41 ] [ 42 ] [ 43 ] and antisemitic views. [ 44 ] [ 45 ] On the left–right political spectrum , it belonged on the right wing . [ 46 ] [ 47 ] Specifically, it is classified as far-right in its early years and then again in the late 1920s when it moved back rightward. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] It has also been described as proto-fascist . [ 18 ]
